original_value: Recent years have witnessed rapid developments on social recommendation techniques for improving the performance of recommender systems due to the growing influence of social networks to our daily life. The majority of existing social recommendation methods unify user representation for the user-item interactions (item domain) and user-user connections (social domain). However, it may restrain user representation learning in each respective domain, since users behave and interact differently in the two domains, which makes their representations to be heterogeneous. In addition, most of traditional recommender systems can not efficiently optimize these objectives, since they utilize negative sampling technique which is unable to provide enough informative guidance towards the training during the optimization process. In this paper, to address the aforementioned challenges, we propose a novel deep adversarial social recommendation framework DASO. It adopts a bidirectional mapping method to transfer users' information between social domain and item domain using adversarial learning. Comprehensive experiments on two real-world datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

result.paraphrase: Recent years have seen swift progress in social recommendation methods aimed at improving recommender system performance, driven by the increasing impact of social networks on daily life. Most existing social recommendation approaches learn a single user representation for both user-item interactions in the item domain and user-user links in the social domain. However, this can limit representation learning in each domain, because users act and interact differently across the two domains, making their representations heterogeneous. Moreover, most traditional recommender systems cannot optimize these objectives efficiently, since they rely on negative sampling, which does not provide sufficiently informative guidance during training optimization. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes DASO, a new deep adversarial social recommendation framework. It uses a bidirectional mapping strategy with adversarial learning to transfer user information between the social and item domains. Extensive experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness.
